target:
def Target : Prop :=
  ∀ (Fm S : Type) [LogicalConnective Fm] [LogicalNeutral Fm] [Entailment S Fm] (𝓢 : S) [Entailment.Cl 𝓢]
    (T K D : Fm → Fm) (σ X G : Fm),
    Def7 𝓢 D T → Def8 𝓢 D K →
    𝓢 ⊢ ∼D σ →
    𝓢 ⊢ ∼D (σ 🡒 X) ⋏ ∼D (K (σ 🡒 G))
translation: Target is the proposition asserting that for every type Fm of sentences equipped with logical connectives (🡒, ⋏, ⋎, ∼) and logical constants (⊤, ⊥), every type S of proof systems equipped with an entailment (provability) relation ⊢ between systems in S and sentences in Fm, every proof system 𝓢 in S that proves all classical propositional tautologies in these connectives and is closed under modus ponens, every triple of arbitrary functions T, K, D : Fm → Fm, and every triple of sentences σ, X, G in Fm: if (1) Def7 𝓢 D T holds—that is, for all sentences φ, ψ in Fm, 𝓢 proves the object-language biconditional D (φ 🡒 ψ) 🡘 (D φ ⋏ (T φ 🡒 D ψ)) (where A 🡘 B abbreviates (A 🡒 B) ⋏ (B 🡒 A))—and (2) Def8 𝓢 D K holds—that is, for every sentence φ in Fm, 𝓢 proves D (K φ) 🡘 D φ—and (3) 𝓢 proves ∼(D σ), then 𝓢 proves the conjunctive sentence ∼(D (σ 🡒 X)) ⋏ ∼(D (K (σ 🡒 G))). Nothing else is assumed: in particular, 𝓢 is not required to be consistent, none of Def1 through Def6 are assumed, T, K, and D are arbitrary functions on sentences subject only to (1) and (2), and σ, X, and G are arbitrary sentences with no additional conditions.

divergences.description: Theorem 7 in Koellner (2018, Part II, p. 467) unconditionally asserts that the concrete system DTK proves the indeterminacy of the specific sentences 'K = F_e → F_e+ ⊆ T' and 'K(K = F_e → G(F_e+))'. The TARGET instead formalizes a more general conditional reduction for an arbitrary classical system 𝓢 and arbitrary sentences σ, X, G, taking 𝓢 ⊢ ∼D σ as a premise rather than formalizing DTK, the internal structure of those sentences, or the proof from Koellner (2016) that 'K = F_e' is provably indeterminate. This reduction is explicitly acknowledged in the author's claim.

Because arithmetic, Gödel coding, and object-language quantifiers are not modelled (a declared limitation), Def7 and Def8 represent axioms (D4) and (D7) as meta-level schemas over an arbitrary sentence type Fm rather than single universally quantified object-language axioms over sentence codes (with Sent(x) ∧ Sent(y) guards in (D4)). Likewise, D is an arbitrary function Fm → Fm rather than being defined as T(x) ∨ T(¬x). These weaken the hypotheses and thus yield a harmlessly more general conditional statement.

Theorem 7 lists two separate provability claims (1) and (2), whereas the TARGET proves their object-language conjunction ∼D (σ 🡒 X) ⋏ ∼D (K (σ 🡒 G)). Under classical propositional logic ([Entailment.Cl 𝓢]), this is logically equivalent to proving each conjunct separately.

judgement.summary: The Lean TARGET faithfully formalizes the author's claimed reduction of Theorem 7: Def7 and Def8 match axioms (D4) and (D7) schematically, and the conclusion matches the two indeterminacy statements of Theorem 7 given the indeterminacy of σ ('K = F_e'). The only divergences are minor idealizations inherent in the declared abstract, quantifier-free setting and the fact that the statement is a conditional reduction rather than Theorem 7 itself.
